# AI Prompts for Novel Writing: The Formula That Actually Works

Most writers type “write me a fantasy novel” and get garbage. The real skill isn’t which AI tool you pick — it’s knowing exactly how to ask. This guide gives you the 4-part formula, copy-paste templates, and the craft moves that separate a publishable draft from the slop filling every writing forum right now.

By the BestPrompt.Art editorial team · April 2026 · 14 min read

fiction writing prompt engineering ChatGPT & Claude character development

TL;DR — The Quick Answer

The single most effective AI prompt for novel writing follows the RCIC formula: Role + Context + Instruction + Constraints. Pair it with iterative refinement — treat every AI output as a first draft, not a final one — and you’ll produce usable fiction faster than you thought possible. The templates below are ready to copy and customize.

Here’s the thing nobody tells you about writing fiction with AI: the tool is almost irrelevant. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Sudowrite — they all fail the same way when you give them bad prompts. Vague input, vague output. Every time.

I’ve watched writers spend months frustrated with AI-generated chapters that sounded hollow, characters that felt like Wikipedia summaries, dialogue no human would ever speak. And every single time, the problem wasn’t the model. It was the prompt construction. Fix that, and the quality jump is immediate and dramatic.

This guide cuts straight to what works. No padding, no theory lectures. Just the framework, the templates, and the specific craft moves that make the difference.
